clue.text: Brace of gulls circling small residence

indicators.note: circling says the dupes go right round the abbreviated home

parts.note: a gull is a dupe, someone made the target of a trick, so gulls are butts
RES is a short form of residence, as in the estate agents' 'des res'

explanation.surface: A pair of seagulls wheeling round a little house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brace of gulls' reads as a pair of birds, but 'Brace' alone is the definition and 'gulls' is a plural noun meaning dupes.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a support, and this is a projecting masonry support propping up a wall.

clue.text: Strut beginning to loosen being wrenched out in gale

indicators.note: being wrenched out says a letter is pulled away from the swaggering word

parts.note: to strut is to swagger, and to bluster is to swagger and talk big

indicators.note: beginning to selects only the opening letter of loosen

explanation.surface: A supporting strut starts to work loose, wrenched out in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes L from 'loosen', and 'being wrenched out' removes it from BLUSTER. 'Strut' reads as a beam but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong blow or storm wind, as in Australia's 'southerly buster', is a gale.

clue.text: Guys grabbing spade tricks

indicators.note: grabbing has the teasing word hold the single letter within it

parts.note: to guy is to mock, and to twit is to tease
S stands for spades in card games

explanation.surface: Some blokes grab a spade to perform tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' looks like men but is the verb meaning mocks (TWITS), which takes in S.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceptions, ruses and surprising turns are tricks, as in a plot's unexpected turns.

clue.text: Bank note turning up in jacket

parts.note: a reef is a bank of rock or sand under the sea

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the note is read from bottom to top

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A banknote turns up in a jacket pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank note' reads as money but is two pieces; 'turning up' turns the note round to give ER at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A short double-breasted jacket worn by sailors, a type of jacket.

clue.text: Steady weather set to change

indicators.note: set to change means the letters are about to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Settled weather looks set to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges WEATHER SET; 'Steady' looks like an adjective about weather but is the noun for a regular partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is someone's regular boyfriend or girlfriend, a beloved.

clue.text: Horror, facing northern river that's polluted

parts.note: a naughty child is called a little horror or an imp
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Something dreadful faces a river in the north of England that is full of pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' just puts the two pieces side by side; the river is the Ure in Yorkshire, a common crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: Something polluted is contaminated, not clean or pure in substance.

clue.text: Smash up some rocks with head of the monkey

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil, smash up

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the letters of some are disturbed
head of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone smashes some rocks against the head of a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like stones but shakes SOME into MOSE; 'head of' gives T from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small South American primate with a long tail is a kind of monkey.

clue.text: Going, using metro?

explanation.surface: Is the journey happening, on the underground?
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: travelling by metro is going by the way under the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in progress or moving is going; travelling by subway train uses a route beneath the streets.

clue.text: Joined bridge players and made a start

parts.note: E and N are East and North, two of the four players at bridge
to get rolling is to make a start

explanation.surface: Someone joined a bridge club and made a start at the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points, so any two of N, E, S, W can stand for them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be signed up as a member of a course or club is to have joined it.

clue.text: Like pest marauding in inflorescence

indicators.note: marauding suggests wild disorderly roving, so the letters of the two words run riot

explanation.surface: Something like a pest marauding inside a flower cluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marauding' shuffles the letters of LIKE PEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical term: a small spike forming part of a grass flower head, itself a flower cluster.

clue.text: About to cut back with clipper, say

indicators.note: back turns the whole run of the two pieces round so it is read from the end

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a business letter
to cut can mean to run off quickly, as in 'cut and run', which is to dart

explanation.surface: Someone about to trim the back of a head with clippers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses RE + DART together, giving the letters in the order T R A D E R. 'clipper' looks like a hair trimmer but is the fast sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipper was a fast merchant sailing ship, an example of a vessel engaged in commerce.

clue.text: Request from English doctor in New York

indicators.note: in places the verb for doctoring inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: to doctor a patient is to treat them

explanation.surface: A request coming from an English physician working in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' reads as a noun but is a verb here, and 'in' sets it within the city's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest plea or appeal is a request.

clue.text: Reddish-brown salad herb

explanation.surface: A salad herb that is reddish-brown in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a reddish-brown horse colour and also a sharp-tasting leaf plant used in salads.

clue.text: One's beaten, blotto on spirit

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: kettled is British slang for very drunk, as blotto is
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone beaten up, blind drunk on spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's beaten' reads as a defeated person, but it means an object struck, a large drum.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large orchestral drum played with sticks, so an instrument that is struck.

clue.text: A green tree spreading with new life

indicators.note: spreading suggests the letters fanning out and settling in a new order

explanation.surface: A green tree spreading its branches as spring brings fresh growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges the ten letters of A GREEN TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means reborn or renewed, given fresh spiritual or physical vigour.

clue.text: Lose short game in which a mate proves uncongenial

definitions.text: in which a mate proves uncongenial

indicators.note: short means the word for lose is docked of its last letter

parts.note: to miss a chance is to lose it
a match is a game

explanation.surface: Losing a brief game in which a partner proves disagreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims MISS to MIS. The definition describes an ill-assorted pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: A poorly suited pairing, as of partners who do not get on, is an unhappy coupling.

clue.text: Painter of arms inscribing old name in coat

indicators.note: in puts the two abbreviations inside the jacket

parts.note: a blazer is a coat or jacket

explanation.surface: A heraldic artist writing an old name in a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' suggests a coat of arms but is the jacket BLAZER; 'inscribing' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To blazon is to describe or paint heraldic arms, so this is a heraldic painter.

clue.text: Light eastern article, authentic

parts.note: the is the definite article
real means authentic, genuine

explanation.surface: A light eastern piece of writing that rings true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a piece of writing but is the grammatical word THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate and airy, as if of the upper air, so light.

clue.text: Not too clever, note, in one estimate?

definitions.text: Not too clever, note, in one estimate?

parts.note: in British idiom 'not too clever' means feeling unwell, that is ill

indicators.note: in places the musical note inside the pair formed by the numeral and the valuation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to rate something is to estimate its worth
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone judged rather dim, at least in one person's estimate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not too clever' is British slang for poorly; 'in' puts the note within one plus estimate. The whole clue also describes someone unable to read, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to read or write, and loosely ignorant or poorly educated, hence not clever in some eyes.

clue.text: Fabric with the Spanish-style beam

parts.note: lint is a fabric for dressing wounds
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Fabric draped over a Spanish-style beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal support across the top of a door or window is a beam.

clue.text: Set in state, in the manner of Solomon

indicators.note: in puts the word for set inside the word for state

parts.note: to state is to say
a jelly sets, or gels, when it firms

explanation.surface: Settled in state, ruling as Solomon did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a nation but is a verb, and 'in' sets the word for set within it.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon is a byword for wisdom, so acting like him means wisely.

clue.text: Spring can make a fellow vocal

indicators.note: vocal means the slang word for a fellow is spoken aloud

parts.note: a geezer is British slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: Spring weather can make a chap talkative.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the hot spring and the water heater are both said like GEEZER, slang for a bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural hot spring that shoots water into the air, as in Iceland.

clue.text: Sail is reportedly in pieces

indicators.note: in puts the spoken word inside the chess figures

parts.note: chessmen are pieces, so pieces gives MEN

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is is rendered as it is heard, with a buzzing z sound

parts.note: the word is is pronounced with a z sound

explanation.surface: A sail is said to be torn to shreds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pieces' suggests a wrecked sail, but 'pieces' are chessmen, and 'reportedly' gives 'is' as heard, with its buzzing z, set 'in' them.
explanation.definitionFit: The aftmost mast of a ship, and the fore-and-aft sail set on it.

clue.text: Remove thatch from crumbling pile in time

indicators.note: in tells us the reworked heap goes inside the calendar word

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: crumbling means the word pile breaks up and its letters re-form

explanation.surface: Stripping a roof of its thatch before the pile crumbles in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbling' rearranges the pile into EPIL, which 'in' sets within the calendar word. 'thatch' is jocular for a head of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To depilate is to strip hair from the body, and 'thatch' is a humorous word for hair.

clue.text: Move somewhere, with Queen vulnerable

parts.note: to tend is to move or incline in some direction
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Someone shifting position while the Queen is exposed to danger.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, from Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sore or sensitive, easily hurt, is vulnerable.

clue.text: Trifles, fruity concoctions

explanation.surface: Light trifles, sweet fruit-based concoctions for dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifles' looks like the pudding but is the verb: one who trifles away time wastes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle away money or time is to waste it bit by bit; battered apple or banana pieces deep-fried are dessert concoctions.

clue.text: Messenger makes a line into crowd

indicators.note: into puts the article and the abbreviation inside the word for a throng

parts.note: a herd is a crowd, especially of animals or people

explanation.surface: A messenger pushes his way in a line into the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link word; A + L goes into HERD.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically an official bearer of royal proclamations, so a messenger.

clue.text: An engaging person

parts.note: reads as someone charming, but means one who engages, that is hires, staff

explanation.definitionFit: A boss who engages workers, taking them on for wages, is literally an engaging person.
